conventions: minchah is headed on 'offering' in all 15 units of the chapter ('meal offering', 'of a meal offering', 'the meal offering'). Rule 31's tie-break decides it: the ASV writes a bare 'offering' for minchah (GEN.4.3-5, MAL.3.4, 1CH.16.29) and never a bare 'meal', so 'meal' is the ASV's specifier and 'offering' the word realizing the lexeme. This is a deliberate divergence from the corpus majority, which heads the two-word phrase on 'meal' in about 32 units against 11 on 'offering'; each unit names the competing reading. Do not harmonize toward the majority without new evidence about how the ASV writes the word alone.

soleth -> 'fine flour' is headed on 'fine' in all five units (vv1, 2, 4, 5, 7). The ASV never writes a bare 'flour' for a Hebrew word of this class - it writes 'meal' for qemach - so 'flour' is the supplied generic under rule 31 and the tie-break does not rescue it. The competing head on 'flour' is named in every unit note.

isheh -> 'an offering made by fire' is headed on 'fire' in all six units (vv2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 16), on rule 31's own olah -> 'burnt offerings' analogy: 'offering' alone is any offering. Where the phrase also carries the clause's copula ('it is an offering made by fire', v16) that copula joins the same unit under rule 20 and does not move the head.

Vessel and grain words: machavat -> 'baking pan' and marchesheth -> 'frying pan' head on 'pan' (vv5, 7); aviv -> 'grain in the ear' and karmel -> 'the fresh ear' head on 'ear' (v14); geres -> 'bruised grain' heads on 'bruised' (vv14, 16), 'grain' being the generic the ASV also supplies inside 'grain in the ear'. The working test across the chapter is whether the shared English noun is the ASV's own rendering of the Hebrew word ('pan', 'ear', 'offering') or a word it writes for something the Hebrew does not name ('grain', 'flour', 'thing', 'fruits'). The vv5/7 note cites the shared class noun instead; the firmer ground is EZK.4.3, where 'an iron pan' renders machavat by a bare 'pan'.

kol ... lo rendered by a single 'No'/'no' (v11, both clauses) is read as one rule 30/35 fusion covering both morphemes, headed on the negative and discontinuous across the intervening relative clause. The article of hamminchah in that phrase is then unrepresented under rule 29, since the ASV writes no 'the' for the phrase. Where a second kol stands with no negative of its own it takes the 'any' the ASV writes for it (rule 15), and the waw of the coordinated member takes the 'nor'.

The definite object marker takes an English word only where the ASV writes one for the object relation on the very phrase the marker stands on: 'as' at v2 ('shall burn it as the memorial thereof') and 'for' at v14 ('shalt offer for the meal offering of thy first fruits'). It is unrepresented at vv6, 8, 9, 12 and 16, where the object is written bare. The resumptive 'it' of 'shall burn it' is added at v2 and v9: no object morpheme stands in either clause, and it does not join the verb merely by standing inside its rendering (rules 44, 30).

The second lamed of 'shall be Aaron's and his sons' (vv3, 10) is unrepresented: the possessive lamed heading the predicate carries the copula under rule 49, but the ASV coordinates the second member bare, writing neither a second copula nor a preposition for it, and the waw already has the 'and'. BSB attaches that lamed to its phrase; that is the documented convention difference and not an error.
report: Checked all 30 candidate groups end to end. Every multi-treatment bucket is an ASV-licensed difference, not a split: the waw follows what the ASV wrote (v12 'but', v4 'or', v11 'nor', 'And'/'and' elsewhere); mem-preposition -> 'of' (vv2, 3, 10) / 'from' (v9) / 'part of' (v16, twice); al -> 'upon' (vv1, 15) / 'with' (vv2, 13, 16) / 'of' (v5); el -> 'unto' (v8) / 'on' (v12); ki -> 'when' (vv1, 4) / 'for' (v11); the 3fs suffix -> 'it' / 'thereof' / 'of it' (v16). The two verbatim-identical verses, 3 and 10, agree unit for unit and head for head.

The added units are what the lemma table cannot see, so I read the dump for them. The chapter's only two are the supplied 'it' of 'shall burn it' at v2 and v9, analysed the same way in both. No supplied English is folded into a neighbouring licensor elsewhere: v11's 'as', v12's 'As', v6's 'in pieces' and the 'of fine flour' of vv1, 4, 5, 7 all go to nominals under rule 33, and the object marker takes an English word only at v2 ('as') and v14 ('for'), where it stands on the very phrase that word introduces, against bare objects at vv6, 8, 9, 12, 16. The hierarchy - a present marker before a rule 33 supply - is applied consistently.

Head choices on modifier-plus-generic phrases are uniform per lexeme and every contested one names its competing reading (rule 8), so nothing is patched. Two deserve flagging. minchah is headed on 'offering' in all 15 units, against a corpus that heads the two-word phrase on 'meal' by roughly 32 to 11; the chapter is nonetheless right under rule 31's tie-break, because the ASV writes a bare 'offering' for minchah (GEN.4.3-5, MAL.3.4, 1CH.16.29, and 15 corpus units) and never a bare 'meal'. Recorded as a convention so a later chapter does not silently revert it.

The weaker ground is at vv5 and 7, which head 'baking pan'/'frying pan' on 'pan' because the ASV uses 'pan' for both machavat and marchesheth. That is not the condition rule 31 states - the tie-break wants the noun written alone for the word - and by this chapter's own reasoning about 'grain' (v14, v16) a noun shared across two renderings is evidence of a supplied generic, which points the other way. The head still stands on a better ground the note did not give: 'pan' is the ASV's own rendering of machavat at EZK.4.3 ('an iron pan', where 'iron' renders barzel), which is rule 31's 'ordinary rendering of the word before you'. Confirm with LEMMA=machavat when EZK.4 is reconciled; no unit here depends on it, and I did not spend the evidence round on two heads that carry their competing reading.

BSB: all six disagreements are convention differences and none is an error. The second lamed of 'shall be Aaron's and his sons' (vv3, 10) has no English at all - the ASV coordinates the second member bare - so rule 40 marks it unrepresented while BSB attaches it to its phrase. min plus suffix at v11 is wholly unrendered ('any' there answers to the kol on 'honey' under rule 15), and its two morphemes are marked separately under rule 2. The article of hamminchah at v11 is unrepresented because the ASV writes no 'the' for the phrase (rule 29; the determiner slot is filled by the fused 'No'). The marker at v12 stands on a bare object ('offer them'), rule 16.

Conventions: 7 recorded. The validation report's other 24 repeated notes restate contract rules ('Waw takes And', 'Divine name', 'Suffix takes the possessive pronoun', the assimilated article, and so on) and are left unlogged deliberately.

No promotion and no amendment. The one construction the contract had not met head-on - kol plus lo collapsed into a single 'No' (v11, twice) - is already inside rule 35, which names kol asher -> 'whatsoever' as a fusion and directs a pass to expect more fusion rather than new rules; writing it again would be a restatement. And the minchah head, the only other general lesson here, is contradicted by the corpus majority, so it must stay a chapter convention and not become a rule.
